metadata.title: Configure Basic PWA Manifest and Metadata

story.iWant: to set up the basic PWA manifest and app metadata
story.soThat: the app can be installed and has proper identity across platforms
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Create PWA manifest using Next.js 16 metadata API (AC: 1) - Create app/manifest.ts file - Define app name: "Will It Rain" - Define short_name: "Will It Rain" - Define description: "Get a simple yes or no answer for the next 24 hours" - Set start_url to "/" - Set display mode to "standalone" - Define background_color: "#0a0a0a" (from UX spec) - Define theme_color: "#0a0a0a" (from UX spec)
- Task 2: Generate and configure app icons (AC: 1) - Create public/icons/ directory - Generate 192x192 app icon (Android home screen) - Generate 512x512 app icon (Android splash) - Generate maskable icon for Android adaptive icons (512x512) - Define icons array in manifest with proper sizes and purpose - Ensure icon paths are correct (public/icons/*)
- Task 3: Configure favicon (AC: 1) - Generate favicon.ico file - Place in public/ directory - Verify favicon loads in browser tab - Test across Chrome, Safari, Firefox
- Task 4: Link manifest in root layout (AC: 1) - Verify Next.js 16 auto-links manifest.ts (no manual linking needed) - Add metadata configuration to app/layout.tsx if needed - Verify manifest is accessible at /manifest.webmanifest
- Task 5: Validate PWA configuration (AC: 1) - Run Lighthouse PWA audit - Verify manifest validates without errors - Check that all required manifest fields are present - Confirm icons load correctly - Test manifest on both development and production builds

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC 1: **Given** the app should work as a Progressive Web App **When** I configure PWA basics **Then** a web app manifest file is created with app metadata **And** manifest includes app name, short name, description **And** theme colors are defined **And** display mode is set to "standalone" **And** manifest is linked in the root layout **And** basic app icons are generated (at least 192x192 and 512x512) **And** favicon is configured

notes.note: Next.js 16.0.1 confirmed (actual version in package.json) - native manifest.ts support included
React 19.2.0 confirmed - latest stable version with concurrent features
TypeScript 5.x with strict mode enforced via tsconfig.json
Tailwind CSS v4 with native PostCSS plugin (no separate config needed)
NO PWA-specific dependencies needed - Next.js handles manifest generation natively

constraints.constraint: Use Next.js 16 native manifest.ts file-based approach - NO external PWA plugins (next-pwa, etc.)
TypeScript strict mode enforced - all code must be strictly typed with proper interfaces
Manifest file MUST export MetadataRoute.Manifest type from next package
Theme colors MUST match UX spec: background_color and theme_color both set to #0a0a0a
Display mode MUST be "standalone" for native app feel (per architecture decision)
Icons MUST include purpose tags: "any" for standard icons, "maskable" for adaptive Android icons
Icon files MUST be PNG format and stored in public/icons/ directory
Minimum icon sizes REQUIRED: 192x192 (Android home) and 512x512 (Android splash)
Favicon MUST be placed in app/ directory (Next.js 16 convention) NOT public/
For Epic 1: Simple placeholder icons sufficient - professional branding deferred to Epic 4 Story 4.5
All file paths in manifest MUST be relative to public directory (e.g., /icons/icon-192.png)
Project structure MUST follow architecture conventions: app/ for application code, public/ for static assets
NO automated tests required for Epic 1 (per tech spec) - manual validation only

tests.standards:
For Epic 1, no automated tests are required (per tech spec). All validation is manual and focuses on: 1. TypeScript compilation (npx tsc --noEmit) - ensures type safety 2. ESLint validation (npm run lint) - ensures code quality 3. Lighthouse PWA audit - validates manifest structure and accessibility 4. Manual browser testing - confirms icons, favicon, and theme colors display correctly 5. Cross-browser validation - test on Chrome, Safari, Firefox for compatibility
Testing approach follows progressive enhancement: validate foundation works before adding complexity. Manual checks ensure PWA basics are correctly configured before moving to advanced PWA features in Epic 4.

test.description: Verify manifest.ts file creation and structure

ideas.test: - Create will-it-rain/app/manifest.ts file - Confirm it exports default function returning MetadataRoute.Manifest - TypeScript compilation passes without errors - Manifest includes all required fields: name, short_name, description, start_url, display, background_color, theme_color, icons

- name: "Will It Rain" - short_name: "Will It Rain" - description: "Get a simple yes or no answer for the next 24 hours" - start_url: "/" - display: "standalone" - background_color: "#0a0a0a" - theme_color: "#0a0a0a"

- public/icons/ directory exists - icon-192.png exists with 192x192 dimensions - icon-512.png exists with 512x512 dimensions - maskable-icon.png exists with 512x512 dimensions and proper safe zone - All icons are PNG format - Icons array in manifest.ts correctly references all three icons
- favicon.ico exists in app/ directory (Next.js 16 convention) - Favicon displays in browser tab when running dev server - Favicon displays correctly across Chrome, Safari, Firefox

- Start dev server (npm run dev) - Navigate to localhost:3000/manifest.webmanifest - Manifest JSON displays with all configured fields - No manual linking required in layout.tsx (Next.js 16 auto-links)

- Run Lighthouse PWA audit in Chrome DevTools - Manifest validation passes without errors - Icons are accessible and properly formatted - Theme color applies on mobile browsers - Display mode "standalone" recognized

- npm run build completes without errors - Production build includes manifest at .next/server/app/manifest.webmanifest - npm run start serves production build successfully - Manifest accessible in production mode
